concepts.title: Properties of Square Numbers
concepts.definition: Square numbers end only in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9 at the units place, never in 2, 3, 7 or 8; they carry an odd number of factors, sit between consecutive squares in growing gaps of odd numbers, and squares of even numbers are even.
concepts.key_idea: The units digit can reject a square instantly but can never confirm one.

solution_steps.explain: Subtract 1, 3, 5 ... ; reaching exactly 0 proves a perfect square.
Pairing prime factors into equal pairs confirms the square.

concepts.title: Pythagorean Triplets
concepts.definition: For any odd natural number m, the three numbers m, half of m squared minus 1, and half of m squared plus 1 form a Pythagorean triplet - taking m = 3 gives the classic 3, 4, 5 satisfying the square-sum relation.
concepts.key_idea: Pick an odd m, then (m*m - 1)/2 and (m*m + 1)/2 complete the triplet.
question_patterns: find a Pythagorean triplet whose one member is 7

solution_steps.explain: Half of sq minus 1 and half of sq plus 1 give the other members.

concepts.title: Squares as Sum of Successive Odd Numbers
concepts.definition: Each square equals the sum of the first so-many odd numbers - 1, 4 = 1 + 3, 9 = 1 + 3 + 5 - so adding the next odd number hops from one square to the next, and successive subtraction of odd numbers tests whether a number is a square.
concepts.key_idea: The nth odd number is 2n - 1, and squares grow by exactly that much.
question_patterns: express 49 as the sum of successive odd numbers

solution_steps.explain: Each square exceeds the previous one by the nth odd number.

concepts.title: Finding the Square of a Number
concepts.definition: Squares of awkward numbers come easy after splitting: write the number as a convenient sum like 43 = 40 + 3 and expand (a + b) squared into a squared + 2ab + b squared, computing each easy piece separately.
concepts.formula: value = a * a + 2 * a * b + b * b
concepts.key_idea: Split, square the parts, double the cross product: 43 squared from 40 and 3.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh105.txt section 5.4 (finding the square of a number, other patterns)

solution_steps.explain: Compute a squared and b squared.
The identity completes the square of the sum.

concepts.title: Square Roots
concepts.definition: The square root undoes squaring: the root of 625 is 25 because 25 squared makes 625; roots are found by repeated subtraction of odd numbers, by pairing prime factors, or by the long division method, and decimals root the same way.
concepts.key_idea: Root asks: which number squared gives this? Pairing factors answers it.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh105.txt section 5.5 (square roots, finding square roots, division method)

solution_steps.explain: The root is the number whose square gives the original.
